author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Greater Boston is expected to begin the weekend with two dry, sunny days before a more organized rain system arrives Sunday. Friday and Saturday should feature gentle breezes, cool starts in the 50s and afternoon highs in the mid-70s, according to NBC10 Boston meteorologists.

Rain is forecast to spread into the region early Sunday and continue into at least part of the afternoon. Current guidance points to roughly three-quarters of an inch to one inch across much of the area, though exact totals and the timing of the final showers remain subject to change.

The Sunday system could be the most substantial rain opportunity in the next seven to 10 days. That makes the dry window on Friday and Saturday the more dependable period for outdoor plans, while drivers and event organizers should prepare for wet roads and reduced visibility as the system moves through.

Humidity will increase with the rain and then fall behind it. Sunshine and a gradual warmup are expected early next week. Residents should still check an updated local forecast before Sunday travel because small shifts in the storm track could change when the heaviest rain arrives and how quickly conditions improve.
dek: Friday and Saturday should stay dry with highs in the mid-70s before a widespread rain system moves through early Sunday.
headline: Boston forecast calls for sunny start before Sunday soaking
